records.title: Pixel-art kit: ramps, auto-shaded sprites, dither, pixel-perfect canvas
records.summary: shadeSprite(rows, ramps) lights and outlines a letter-map sprite (top-left light, selective outline, white hit-flash copy; scale 2 for twice the detail, scale 4 for four times: round corners and smooth nine-shade light); ramp(base) makes a hue-shifted 5-shade ramp; RAMPS ready-made; dither/bayer; pixelCanvas(screen) low-res layer at whole-number zoom; paintGround; pixelEllipse; hardAlpha.

records.title: Pixel effect player: any of 244 effects on a canvas or a three.js texture
records.summary: playFx(id, {palette, seed, flip, angle}) loads one effect on demand and returns a player: update(dt), canvas, origin, size, done, stop(), texture(THREE). Find ids with `npm run kb -- <words>` (kind pixel-effect).

records.title: Sprite baker: 3D models rendered once into 2D sprite sheets
records.summary: SpriteBaker renders skinned models (soldier ranks, skeletons, robot) from a three-quarter camera into sheets — 5 directions (mirrored for 8), idle/run/walk/attack frames — plus still objects; then the 3D is let go. The classic pre-rendered sprite look at 2D cost.

records.title: Realistic 2D land: photo-textured bands, cliffs, blight, depth-sorted sprites
records.summary: paintLand paints a whole map once (texture bands blended on noise masks, piled-boulder cliffs, walls, scattered props); drawWorld draws shadows then everything back to front; remains() leaves bones and rubble on the land.

records.title: Synthesized game sound and adaptive music (Web Audio)
records.summary: PurgeAudio: effects built from shaped noise and tones (shots, blasts, horn, bell, coins, frost) through a compressor and a short reverb; a step-sequenced score (chords, bass, melody, kick/snare/hats, arpeggio) with calm and battle beds that cross-fade on a fight level; music and sound switches.

records.title: Headless RTS-style simulation with rooms
records.summary: Purge: fixed-step sim with spatial hash, grid A* with corner cutting, group move formations, guard camps that wake and leash, spawners, waves, bunkers, upgrades, bots; snapshot() small enough to send 10×/s; host-run rooms via MobaLink + Mirror interpolation.

records.title: Shared HUD overlay for 2D and 3D views
records.summary: drawOverlay/pickAt/boxedIn work with any view exposing toScreen(x,y,z): health bars, names, popups, box-select, picking — so a game can have a 2D and a 3D view of one simulation.

records.title: Cover-shot script: real screenshots of every game
records.summary: scripts/covers.mjs opens each game in a browser, stages a good moment, hides HUD and saves an 800×450 JPEG to public/covers.

records.title: Asset catalog: query models and materials by theme and kind
records.summary: Catalog.query/pick over library/catalog.json (KayKit, Poly Haven, ambientCG, extras), with categories and themes; everything that places a model goes through it.

records.title: Race courses planned on a real road graph
records.summary: buildGraph + planCourse/planRun: Dijkstra with a heap over OSM roads, used-edge penalty, spur and hairpin cutting; deterministic so every player plans the same course.

records.title: Animation retargeting bone by bone
records.summary: Borrow one rig's idle/walk/run for another skeleton: each bone's turn from rest copied across in each skeleton's own frame.

records.title: Pixel-perfect rendering: draw small, zoom by a whole number
records.summary: Paint the world on a low-resolution canvas (K=2 detail pixels a world unit) and copy it up at an integer zoom with imageSmoothingEnabled=false. Never 2.5×: uneven scaling makes some pixels wider — the commonest reason pixel games look cheap. Round every draw position and the camera (after shake) to whole pixels.

records.title: Colour ramps with hue shifting
records.summary: Each material gets 5 shades, deep shadow to highlight; shadows shift towards blue-violet and highlights towards yellow instead of only darker/lighter. A palette of 24–40 colours in ramps of 4–5.

records.title: One light source, top-left, everywhere
records.summary: Top and left edges take lighter shades, bottom and right darker, on every sprite, tree and rock. The lower part of a shape is a shade darker.

records.title: Selective outlines, not black
records.summary: Each outline pixel is the darkest shade of the colour it touches mixed towards a deep ink; top edges get a lighter outline than bottom edges, which reads as rim light.

records.title: Dithering only on big shapes
records.summary: A 4×4 Bayer pattern blends two shades without a new colour: add the Bayer value before choosing the shade. Use on grass, shadows and large shapes — never on small sprites, where it reads as noise.

records.title: Silhouette first
records.summary: Block the character in one flat colour: if it reads as a dark shape it reads in the game. Big heads, hats and eyes; a 1-pixel white glint in each eye. Judge at real size and speed, never zoomed in.

records.title: Keep text out of the pixel layer
records.summary: Damage numbers, labels and the HUD are drawn at full resolution on top (or in the DOM), so they stay sharp at any zoom.

records.title: Paint the ground once
records.summary: Paint terrain, decorations, contact shadows under trees and sun patches into one big offscreen canvas at load; copy from it each frame. Painting is slow, copying is free.

records.title: Y-sorting and a shadow pass
records.summary: Everything that stands (trees, enemies, the player) goes in one list sorted by foot position each frame; draw all shadows first, then sprites in order, so you can walk behind a tree.

records.title: Every action answers: flash, number, shake, particles
records.summary: A hit gets a sound, a white flash (a pre-made pure-white copy of the sprite for 0.1 s), a damage number and knockback; big actions get screen shake (decaying fast) and particles; small ones get neither.

records.title: Additive blending for light, normal for matter
records.summary: Fire, glows and flashes use globalCompositeOperation='lighter' so overlaps add to white-hot cores; smoke, dirt and debris use normal blending. Fire colour follows a particle's age: white-hot to deep red.

records.title: Cast time sells power
records.summary: A 0.45 s wind-up with a growing magic circle and the caster slowed makes the explosion feel earned. Area hits on a ground seen at an angle are ellipses: divide the vertical distance by ~0.6.

records.title: Colour grade and vignette last
records.summary: Three final passes set the mood: a soft-light warm fill over the pixel layer, a slow breathing sunbeam gradient in screen mode, and a radial vignette.

records.title: Rules for a good pixel effect
records.summary: Lines and light, not fills; hard ramp steps in colour, softness only in light and smoke; fast in, slow out with a 1–2 frame white hero frame; vary every particle; light from one side; let one-shots shrink or dither out; loops seamless; seeded, never Math.random; under 2 ms a frame.

records.title: Pixel-art pass for 3D scenes (general palette, transparent, detail 1–4)
records.summary: pixelPass(renderer, { detail: 4 }) draws any three.js scene as pixel art: inked edges, ordered dither, snapped to a 64-colour palette built from our ramps; see-through background; detail 1 chunky … 4 fine.

records.title: Channels: a maker's space, playlists, play time, badges, mistake reports
records.summary: server/channelStore.js (channels, playlists, play_progress, mistake_reports; public/private with a private-link key; BADGES from stats) and src/ui/ChannelPage.js (video-channel layout: banner, tabs, shelves, play-through view). createPlayTracker counts real play time.

records.title: Rigged characters: meshopt loader, shared-rig clips, retargeting, VRM expressions
records.summary: characterLoader() reads meshopt GLBs (Mesh2Motion); rigClips(loader, catalog, model, names) loads clips that ship as separate files on a shared rig; segmentClips(clip, model.segments) cuts Gobkit's one baked track into idle/walk/attack/dead; retargetClip(target, source, clip, BONE_MAPS.mixamo|kaykit) bakes any of Mesh2Motion's 234 CC0 human clips onto Mixamo, VRM or KayKit bodies (handles A-pose vs T-pose); vrmExpressions/setExpression drive VRM blink and mouth shapes. Guide: knowledge/assets-guide.md.

records.title: Assets guide: best ready characters and creatures, how to load and animate them, how to generate new ones
records.summary: What the library holds (rigged humans, animals, beasts, mounts, cute creatures, VRM avatars, HDRIs), the best pick per use, loading with GLTFLoader + meshopt, AnimationMixer, SkeletonUtils.clone and retargeting, packs to drop in by hand, and generation options (Meshy/Tripo, TRELLIS.2 on Mac, SDF sculpting).

records.title: Shared background music: mood crossfades, seamless loops, stingers, credit toast
records.summary: music.play(idOrTag), music.setMood('calm'|'tense'|'battle'|'boss') with equal-power crossfades (1.5 s into battle, 3 s out; calm/tense pairs start in step with the bar), music.stinger(id) ducking the bed, sample-accurate loops from the manifest's loop points, lazy decode with an LRU cache (and <audio> streaming fallback), autoplay unlock on the first gesture, pause in hidden tabs, saved volume/mute, linkMute(() => sound.muted) to follow a game's own toggle, a '♪ title · Music: ACE-Step 1.5 (MIT)' toast the first time each track plays, credit() and musicCredits(ids) for Credits panels. Tracks: public/audio/bgm (battle, boss, meadow, night forest, village, lantern valley, jungle explore/hunt, frozen fortress, playful kids, synthwave city night, title, and victory/defeat/level-up/discovery stingers). Guide: docs/music.md.

records.title: Making more music: ACE-Step 1.5 on this Mac (free, MIT), looped and mastered
records.summary: npm run music:setup installs ACE-Step 1.5 (MIT code and weights, ungated) into library/tools/ace-step with a uv venv from its lockfile and the 4B XL SFT model; npm run music:gen -- --prompt '…' --seconds 150 --out x.ogg makes takes, judges them (clipping, flat tops, drop-outs, tempo and key vs. the prompt), finds bar-aligned loop points, crossfades the seam, masters to -16 LUFS and writes Ogg Vorbis; npm run music:soundtrack rebuilds public/audio/bgm from scripts/music/soundtrack.json; npm run music:preview to listen.
